title: Annual aberration alone leaves at least 15 arcseconds in nine selected GJ667 header offsets
abstract: We test whether an omitted or extra annual-aberration term explains nine selected broad-profile GJ667 HARPS header offsets. We use twelve cached ESO headers and HARPS-RVBank version 02. Exact relativistic aberration leaves at least 15.67 arcseconds even when each exposure gets its better sign. An alternate proper-motion convention retains large offsets. The exact and first-order shifts differ by less than 0.000476 arcseconds; an exposure-midpoint test changes shifts by less than 0.001849 arcseconds. Annual aberration alone therefore fails within this model. Telescope-control, atmospheric and other frame terms remain open. This does not prove wrong-source acquisition or a planet. No independent observations are supplied. We include code, hashes, aggregate evidence, a figure and external retrieval steps. Raw data and per-exposure tables remain outside the baseline package. Job sci-1107-dell-astronomy-53ab0f3a2664; machine dell; model gpt-6.1-sol.

display.caption: Group ranges and root mean square offsets before and after the best sign of annual aberration for each exposure. All broad profiles retain large offsets.
